placements.why: The envelope introduces a mandatory, signed-manifest gate governing how Meridian deploys move into staging and production — a control over the shape of the delivery pipeline itself, not a product, org, or proof-point theme. No existing strata category exists yet in this repo, and nothing supplied is even close, so this names the organizational category (release/deployment control) that this content and future release-gate content will nest under.
placements.title: Release delivery becomes a gated, verifiable process
placements.frame: What technical control is being imposed on how software moves through environments, and why does that control exist?

placements.title: Meridian deploys must carry verified provenance before they ship
placements.frame: What artifact-level proof is required before a Meridian deploy reaches an environment, who is accountable for it, and what prior failure does it answer to?
placements.why: src-1 (the directive establishing the signed-manifest requirement), src-3/src-4 (the formal Gate/Scope record entries restating and delimiting it to staging and production), src-5 (the named owner accountable for it), and src-2 (the prior-incident fact — two unsigned artifacts reaching staging — that motivates it) are all facets of one recurring subject: what proof a Meridian deploy must carry, where that requirement reaches, and who answers for it. This is a theme future release-train envelopes will keep feeding (new gates, scope changes, ownership handoffs), not a one-time fact — src-2 in particular is evidence supporting the theme rather than a leaf of its own, per the narrative grain test. No existing narrative leaf exists in this repo to hold it, and it sits naturally under the newly-minted Architecture strata as the first content in that category.
